name: Kematen in Tirol
kurzbeschreibung: Dynamic Inn Valley community at the Melach confluence with a unique triple-onion church spire, Martinswand views, and gateway to Kühtai.
beschreibung:
Overview

Kematen in Tirol is situated at an elevation of 610 metres in the Inn Valley within the district of Innsbruck-Land, just twelve kilometres west of the Tyrolean provincial capital Innsbruck. This thriving community of roughly 3,281 residents occupies the alluvial fan of the Melach River, precisely at its confluence with the Inn. Geographically, this river junction marks the boundary between the Upper and Lower Inn Valley. Directly across the northern riverbank, the sheer 700-metre limestone precipice of the Martinswand towers into the sky, creating a breathtaking alpine backdrop. Kematen blends superior residential comfort and proud village traditions with exceptional public transport links. The municipality serves as the primary gateway into the scenic Sellrain Valley and the high-altitude ski resort of Kühtai.

History

Kematen was first documented in 1143 under the name 'Ceminat'. The toponym is derived from the Latin word caminata, denoting a heated room with a fireplace, reflecting early manorial residences. Around 1242, records mention the 'castrum Chemenaten', the ancestor of the later Burghof estate. For centuries, mills powered by the rushing waters of the Melach and traditional farming sustained the village. The Parish Church of Saints Victor and Mary Magdalene was recorded in 1381, expanded in 1686 by master builder Johann Martin Gumpp the Elder, and transformed into a Baroque showpiece by the Umhauser brothers in the eighteenth century. Its bell tower is an architectural marvel unique to Tyrol, boasting a distinctive triple-onion dome. In modern times, Kematen evolved into a bustling business hub, famously housing the headquarters of the historic Ruetz artisanal bakery.

Getting There

Rail connections to Kematen are outstanding: the Kematen in Tirol railway station on the Arlberg rail line is served by S-Bahn commuter routes S1, S2, and S3 as well as regional express trains. Journey time from Innsbruck Central Station is just eleven to thirteen minutes. Drivers reach the town via the Inntal Autobahn A12, using either the Zirl-Ost/Kematen or Völs/Kematen exits, or via the B171 Federal Highway. The L13 Sellraintalstraße branches directly off into Sellrain, Gries, and Kühtai. Regular VVT regional buses link the village smoothly with Innsbruck and neighbouring plateau communities.

Tips

The riverside trails in Kematen provide peerless vantage points for admiring the Martinswand cliff and the legendary Emperor Maximilian Grotto, where legend holds the Habsburg monarch was rescued while hunting chamois. A favourite stop for visitors is the Ruetz Backhaus bakery flagship, featuring traditional wood-fired ovens, a café lounge, and an outdoor terrace on Sportplatzweg. Active travellers appreciate the community sports centre, equipped with tennis courts, beach volleyball, and a modern skatepark. Cyclists can roll effortlessly along the flat Inn Cycle Path R1 beside the river. Throughout the year, Kematen serves as the ideal springboard for alpine adventures into the Sellrain Valley and high-altitude skiing in Kühtai above 2,000 metres.
